key_concepts: Reproduction is the ability of a living thing to continue the existence of its kind.
Animals reproduce through sexual reproduction or asexual reproduction.
Sexual reproduction involves the union of sex cells from two parents.
Male gonads are testes that produce sperm; female gonads are ovaries that produce eggs.
Sperm and egg cells are called gametes.
Fertilization is the union of a sperm cell and an egg cell.
The fertilized egg is called a zygote and develops into an embryo.
Internal fertilization occurs inside the female body, as in dogs and cats.
External fertilization occurs outside the body, usually in water, as in frogs and mosquito
Asexual reproduction involves only one parent producing identical copies, as in sea anemon
Butterflies begin reproduction with courtship and male pheromones.
Mosquitoes lay eggs on or near water and develop through egg, larva, pupa, and adult stage
